messages:
sara: FYI customer acme-prod reported sporadic 500s from /v1/rerank when inputs contain emojis from mobile. they see 500 + 'invalid UTF-8' in our logs. request_id: r-0a1b2c3d
marco: Can you paste the raw body they sent (or sanitized) and a failing request_id? Also which SDK/client?
sara: sent the payload and client info. they use our iOS SDK (v1.4.2) and the app does chunked uploads. sample body (escaped) below:
```
{"queries": ["text1", "text2"], "candidates": ["hello\u0000world", "\uF0\u9F\u98"]}
```
note: the second candidate here shows truncated emoji bytes (last byte missing) because iOS chunk boundary split the multibyte sequence.
marco: runtime log for r-0a1b2c3d:
```
2026-02-14T15:22:11Z ERROR runtime.decode - invalid continuation byte at offset 123
stack: Utf8Error: invalid continuation byte
 at Utf8Decoder.decode (runtime/utf8.rs:78)
 at rerank_service::handler::parse_inputs (rerank.rs:210)
```
marco: looks like our low-level parser uses a strict UTF-8 decoder and throws on malformed sequences, which currently bubbles up as 500. we should return a 4xx with clear message or tolerate by replacing.
jordan: +1 to returning 400 for bad client input. but customer has data already in storage (some records include NUL padding and truncated graphemes from older mobile clients). if we start rejecting, they'll see failures across many jobs.
sre-oncall: they're also seeing retries that spike latency and error budget because retries hit our dedicated rerank pool. priority: avoid cascading retries.
sara: customer wants a path forward: temporary mitigation, suggested repro steps for them, and timeline for a patch.
marco: mitigation options:
- server-side tolerant decode: replace invalid bytes with U+FFFD (�) and proceed (fast, low-risk).
- validate and return 400 with error code INVALID_ENCODING and sample offsets (strict, but forces client fixes).
- SDK patch: update iOS SDK to use streaming TextDecoder-equivalent that preserves partial codepoints across chunks (longer-term).
jordan: for quality we should also add a regression test: payloads with: trailing partial 4-byte emoji (e.g., 0xF0 0x9F 0x98), embedded NULs, and long combining sequences. include rerank scoring sanity checks so truncated graphemes don't wildly change scores.
marco: quick patch plan: add a tolerant decode switch default-on in the parser that replaces invalid sequences, log a distinct metric (encoding.replace_count) and return 200 for now. follow-up: 4xx enforcement behind feature flag and SDK update.
sara: I'll propose that to the customer: temporary tolerant decode to reduce 500s and retries, SDK update + repro guide for next release.
sara: repro steps for them to validate locally:
```
# reproduce broken chunking by truncating a UTF-8 sequence
cat <<EOF > payload.json
{"candidates": ["ok", "\xF0\x9F\x98"]}
EOF
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8" --data-binary @payload.json https://api.redwood.example/v1/rerank
```
marco: thanks. i'll open a runtime PR with the tolerant decoder + metric. tagging @jordan for the regression tests. please set severity P2 for the patch; P1 if customer impact grows.
sara: customer ok with temporary fix; tracking in TICKET-3421. i'll update when they confirm. :white_check_mark:
